_source.name: nkowaokwu/igbo_api
_source.note: Igbo dialect list, grammar classes and tense categories adapted from the Igbo API constants (src/shared/constants/Dialect.ts, WordClass.ts, Tenses.ts). Generalized into the language-scoped dialect/part_of_speech/form_type tables.

partsOfSpeech.name: Adjective
partsOfSpeech.description: An adjective describes a noun. It explains how a noun is.

partsOfSpeech.name: Adverb
partsOfSpeech.description: A describer for how or the extent to which a verb is performed. Eg. nwayọnwayọ, Ikiike, Ọsịịsọ.

partsOfSpeech.name: Active verb
partsOfSpeech.description: A verb that is pure action. Can be stopped and started instantly. Grammatically, it has a clear present/ongoing action. Eg ‘gba’, ‘ri’, ‘ga’ etc can be in the clear present/ongoing form ‘na-agba’, ‘na-eri’, ‘ga-aga’.

partsOfSpeech.name: Medial verb
partsOfSpeech.description: A medial verb is a verb with two present tense concepts. One is inactive/stative, while the other is progressive/active.

partsOfSpeech.name: Passive verb
partsOfSpeech.description: An action that tends to be mostly a situation/state. It is not performative. Its command is always spelled like past tense, though toned like a command while its present tense is always its root. Eg. ‘bụ’, ‘nọ’, ‘bi’ etc are conditions/states and

partsOfSpeech.name: Conjunction
partsOfSpeech.description: A word joins or links two words or two sentences. Eg. Na(And,That), Maka, Ka(That).

partsOfSpeech.name: Demonstrative
partsOfSpeech.description: A word is a pointing word. It shows. Eg. A, Ahụ, Nke, ugbua.

partsOfSpeech.name: Name
partsOfSpeech.description: Person is uniquely called. Eg. Chiọma, Ezenwa, Naịjiria, Amerịka, etc.

partsOfSpeech.name: Noun
partsOfSpeech.description: Used to identify any people, place , or thing. Eg. ụlọ, iko, akwụkwọ.

partsOfSpeech.name: Nominal Modifier
partsOfSpeech.description: Words act similar to the English adjective and noun. They are described as nominal modifiers since they are technically nouns that provide details like adjectives.

partsOfSpeech.name: Proper noun
partsOfSpeech.description: Person/place is uniquely called. Eg. Chiọma, Ezenwa, Naịjiria, Amerịka, etc.

partsOfSpeech.name: Number
partsOfSpeech.description: What any digit or group of digits is called. Otu, Abụọ, Atọ.

partsOfSpeech.name: Preposition
partsOfSpeech.description: This is that word you mention before a location time or person. They cannot just exist on their own. A noun must come before them Eg. Na(In, On, At), mgbe/oge, elu, okpuru, Akụkụ.

partsOfSpeech.name: Pronoun
partsOfSpeech.description: Person/place is uniquely called. Eg. Chiọma, Ezenwa, Naịjiria, Amerịka, etc.

partsOfSpeech.name: Foreign word
partsOfSpeech.description: A word that is known to not be an Igbo word. Mostly does not follow the Igbo words formation pattern.

partsOfSpeech.name: Quantifier
partsOfSpeech.description: A word that shows the amount of something. Niile, Ụfọdụ, Imeriime.

partsOfSpeech.name: Interrogative
partsOfSpeech.description: The typical question tags. Eg. Kedụ?, Ebee?, Olee?, Gịnị?, Ole?.

partsOfSpeech.name: Interjection
partsOfSpeech.description: These are exclamative words. Eg. Ewoo! Okokokoo! Olooo! Chaị! Ee! Mba!

partsOfSpeech.name: Inflectional suffix
partsOfSpeech.description: Explainable parts of a verb that an attached, especially at the beginning of a verb, to create a tense for the verb. They can occur in other contexts as an entirely different part of speech. Eg. I, Ị, O, Ọ, A, E, N, M, Na-, Ga-.

partsOfSpeech.name: Extensional suffix
partsOfSpeech.description: Suffixes attached at the end of a verb to add more meaning to the verbs. They also tend to retain their idea when on their own. Some of them stem from other verbs. Eg. -kwa, -rịrị, -ghị, -la, -kwu, -ju, -pụ, etc.

partsOfSpeech.name: Punctuations
partsOfSpeech.description: These are punctuation marks used in the Igbo language.
